committees.name: Program Self-Assessment Committee (PSAC)
committees.tags: OBE | Accreditation | Academic Quality | Mission & Vision | Stakeholder Feedback | CQI

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Program Self-Assessment Committee (PSAC) is responsible for monitoring, evaluating, and continuously improving the academic programme of the Department in alignment with Outcome-Based Education (OBE), institutional quality-assurance requirements, and applicable accreditation standards.

The PSAC serves as the principal programme-level quality-assurance body for self-assessment, CLO/PLO attainment analysis, stakeholder feedback, Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI), Mission and Vision review, and maintenance of supporting evidence. It also ensures systematic participation of students, alumni, employers/industry representatives, faculty members, and other relevant stakeholders in programme improvement.

Note: BAC standards require curriculum review to include representation from industry/employers and alumni, require a functional alumni association to contribute to quality assurance, and require systematic collection and use of stakeholder feedback for continual improvement.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Programme self-assessment and academic quality assurance.
Implementation and monitoring of the OBE framework.
Review of CLO-PLO alignment, attainment, teaching-learning activities, and assessment methods.
Coordination of OBE implementation and course-file preparation workshops.
Preparation and periodic review of Departmental Mission and Vision statements.
Collection, analysis, and documentation of feedback from students, alumni, employers/industry representatives, faculty members, and other stakeholders.
Coordination with alumni representatives/Alumni Association for quality-assurance activities.
Monitoring and documentation of Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI).
Liaison with the Institutional Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC).
Maintenance of accreditation evidence and support to the BAETE/Accreditation Committee.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead, coordinate, and supervise all PSAC activities.
Prepare semester-wise and annual PSAC activity plans.
Coordinate OBE implementation, course-file preparation, and CQI workshops.
Ensure collection and review of course files, course outlines, CLO-PLO mappings, rubrics, attainment data, and CQI records.
Coordinate preparation of semester-wise and annual self-assessment reports.
Coordinate preparation/revision of Departmental Mission and Vision statements in consultation with the Chairman of the Department and relevant stakeholders.
Ensure systematic collection and analysis of student, alumni, employer, faculty, and stakeholder feedback.
Ensure appropriate alumni and industry participation in curriculum and programme review activities.
Ensure that findings and recommendations are forwarded to the appropriate committee or authority.
Monitor implementation of corrective and improvement actions.
Report PSAC progress and outputs to the IQAC, the Chairman of the Department, and the Departmental Academic Committee.
Coordinate with the BAETE/Accreditation Committee to ensure consistency between self-assessment findings and accreditation documentation.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Assist the Head of the Committee in planning and implementing PSAC activities.
Assist in organising OBE workshops, stakeholder consultations, and quality-assurance activities.
Collect course files, course outlines, CLO-PLO mapping documents, attainment records, rubrics, and supporting evidence.
Review course files for completeness and OBE compliance.
Assist in compiling and analysing CLO/PLO attainment data.
Assist in identifying academic gaps and improvement measures.
Support preparation and review of Mission and Vision statements.
Assist in collecting and analysing feedback from students, alumni, employers/industry, faculty, and other stakeholders.
Assist in alumni surveys, stakeholder consultations, focus-group discussions, and tracer studies where applicable.
Maintain documentary evidence of stakeholder participation and recommendations.
Assist in preparation of self-assessment reports, stakeholder-feedback reports, and CQI action plans.
Monitor assigned CQI actions and maintain supporting records.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Conduct OBE implementation and course-file preparation workshops at the beginning of each semester.
Conduct periodic programme self-assessment using approved institutional/accreditation instruments.
Review alignment among CLOs, PLOs, teaching-learning activities, and assessment methods.
Collect and analyse CLO/PLO attainment data.
Identify areas of under-attainment and develop evidence-based CQI actions.
Review effectiveness of corrective actions from previous cycles.
Prepare semester-wise and annual programme self-assessment and CQI reports.
Prepare and periodically review Departmental Mission and Vision statements.
Establish a systematic mechanism for obtaining stakeholder feedback.
Conduct periodic alumni and employer/industry feedback activities.
Analyse alumni feedback regarding curriculum relevance, graduate competencies, employability, professional preparedness, career progression, and emerging professional requirements.
Facilitate alumni and employer/industry participation in relevant curriculum-review activities.
Forward curriculum-related recommendations to the Syllabus/Curriculum Committee and other recommendations to the appropriate authority.
Maintain evidence showing how stakeholder feedback has contributed to programme improvement.
Maintain the complete programme self-assessment and CQI portfolio.
Coordinate with the BAETE/Accreditation Committee for supporting accreditation evidence.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Prepare semester-wise and annual PSAC plans.
Organise OBE and course-file preparation workshops.
Collect and review course files and OBE documentation.
Prepare the Course File Review Summary.
Compile and analyse CLO/PLO attainment data.
Prepare CQI Action Plans and follow-up reports.
Draft/revise Departmental Mission and Vision statements.
Conduct alumni, student, and employer/industry feedback activities.
Prepare Alumni and Stakeholder Feedback Analysis Reports.
Facilitate alumni/industry representation in curriculum review.
Prepare a Stakeholder Recommendation and Action-Taken Matrix.
Track corrective actions from previous self-assessment cycles.
Prepare and submit programme self-assessment reports to the IQAC.
Maintain records of PSAC activities, meetings, decisions, and evidence.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Academic Cycle → Data Collection → Course File Review → Student/Alumni/Employer/Faculty Feedback → CLO/PLO and Stakeholder Analysis → Identification of Gaps → Programme Self-Assessment Report → CQI Action Plan → Submission/Referral to IQAC and Relevant Committees → Implementation → Follow-up and Effectiveness Review → Next Cycle
Stakeholder Feedback → PSAC Analysis → Curriculum Recommendation → Academic/Syllabus Committee → Decision → Implementation → PSAC Follow-up

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: OBE Workshop agenda, attendance, materials, and summary.
CQI Action Plan and Action-Taken Report.
Revised Mission and Vision statements, where required.
Evidence of alumni/industry participation in curriculum review.
PSAC meeting minutes and activity log.

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: PSAC formation documents and Terms of Reference.
Meeting notices, agendas, attendance, minutes, and resolutions.
CQI plans, implementation records, and action-taken reports.
Alumni survey instruments and feedback reports.
Evidence of alumni/industry participation in curriculum review.
Correspondence with the IQAC and other relevant committees.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the IQAC, the Chairman of the Department, and the Departmental Academic Committee.
Reporting frequency: End of each semester and annually, with additional reporting as required by IQAC or accreditation schedules.

The Head of the Committee is accountable for overall coordination, timely completion of self-assessment activities, quality of reports, stakeholder engagement, and monitoring of CQI actions. Members of the Committee are responsible for assigned data collection, document review, analysis, record keeping, and follow-up activities.
The PSAC shall maintain evidence of the complete quality-improvement cycle:
Finding → Recommendation → Decision → Action → Evidence → Effectiveness Review

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: IQAC: Receives self-assessment, OBE, CQI, and quality-assurance reports and provides institutional guidance.
BAETE/Accreditation Committee: Receives relevant self-assessment, attainment, stakeholder, and CQI evidence for accreditation purposes.
Syllabus/Curriculum Committee: Receives curriculum-related recommendations identified through self-assessment and stakeholder feedback.
Academic Committee: Reviews Mission/Vision proposals, major PSAC findings, and academic recommendations.
Examination Committee: Coordinates on assessment-related evidence and outcome-attainment information.
Teaching Load Committee: Coordinates where necessary to support timely preparation of OBE-compliant course documents.
Alumni Association/Alumni Representatives: Support alumni feedback, consultation, and participation in programme quality-assurance activities.
Industry/Employer Representatives: Provide feedback on curriculum relevance, graduate competencies, employability, and professional requirements.
Faculty Members: Provide course files, attainment records, and CQI evidence.
Students: Provide structured feedback on courses, teaching-learning, and programme effectiveness.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: The PSAC is primarily a programme-level quality-assurance, self-assessment, stakeholder-feedback, and CQI body. It does not duplicate the responsibilities of other committees.
This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Routine examination management (handled by the Examination Committee).
Primary syllabus/curriculum development and approval (handled by the Syllabus/Curriculum Committee); the PSAC may provide evidence-based recommendations.
Direct accreditation application/submission (handled by the BAETE/Accreditation Committee).
Routine teaching-load allocation (handled by the Teaching Load Committee/appropriate authority).
Routine administration of the Alumni Association, including membership, reunions, fundraising, elections, and social activities.
Direct implementation of recommendations assigned to another committee or administrative office.

Note on alumni engagement: The PSAC shall engage alumni only for academic quality assurance, programme review, curriculum feedback, graduate competency evaluation, employability feedback, CQI, and accreditation evidence. The Alumni Association shall remain responsible for general alumni administration and engagement.

committees.name: Examination Committee
committees.tags: Question Papers | Examination Conduct | Scheduling | Records

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Examination Committee is responsible for planning, coordinating and overseeing all aspects of the departmental examination process, from question-paper collection to examination-room management, ensuring integrity, consistency and timely conduct of final and other formal examinations.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Collection, verification and secure handling of question papers.
Coordination of examination schedules and arrangements.
Management of Final Year Design Project (FYDP) evaluation schedules (FYDP I, II, III).
Enforcement of examination-conduct protocols, including faculty presence requirements.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead and coordinate the Examination Committee's activities and ensure examination-related deadlines are met.
Oversee collection and secure handling of question papers, including verification of signatures.
Coordinate FYDP pre-defense, demo defense and final defense schedules.
Submit examination-related reports to the Chairman of the Department and escalate irregularities as needed.
Serve as the primary point of coordination with the Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee following each examination cycle.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Notify Faculty Members of question-paper submission deadlines.
Collect question papers (hard copy and soft copy) and verify signatures.
Maintain the secure submission register and arrange A3-size envelopes.
Brief Executive Officers and Laboratory Assistants on logistical duties.
Collect and file FYDP evaluation reports from supervisors and distribute plagiarism-screening guidelines.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The deadline for submission of Final Examination question papers each semester is set and communicated by the Committee.
Faculty Members must submit both hard copies and soft copies of their question papers to the Examination Committee.
All hard-copy question papers must bear the Faculty Member's signature on the reverse side; for multi-page question papers, each page must be printed separately and signed individually.
Executive Officers and Laboratory Assistants provide logistical support; however, the respective course teacher must remain present throughout the examination period.
A3-size envelopes are used for all examination question papers to ensure safe handling and confidentiality of examination materials.
The Abstract, Conclusion, and Future Work sections of all FYDP reports are screened using plagiarism-detection software before the final defense.
Finalized report templates for FYDP I and FYDP II, standardized presentation templates, and presentation guidelines are provided to students before the pre-defense.
FYDP III report templates and presentation guidelines are prepared and distributed before the relevant defense sessions.
FYDP defense schedules (pre-defense, demo defense, final defense) are set and communicated for each batch.
FYDP supervisors submit evaluation reports to the Examination Committee by the communicated deadline.
Prepare and distribute the examination schedule at least two weeks before the commencement of examinations.
Maintain an examination room allocation and invigilator assignment plan.
Coordinate with the Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee for timely result processing.
Maintain records of all submitted question papers and examination materials.
Prepare post-examination reports on irregularities (if any) for submission to the Chairman of the Department.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Notify Faculty Members of question-paper submission deadlines.
Collect question papers (hard copy and soft copy) and verify signatures.
Arrange A3-size envelopes and label them by course/section.
Prepare the final examination room schedule and communicate it to Faculty Members.
Brief Executive Officers and Laboratory Assistants on their logistical duties.
Coordinate FYDP pre-defense, demo defense and final defense schedules.
Distribute plagiarism-screening guidelines to FYDP supervisors.
Collect and file FYDP evaluation reports from supervisors.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Examination Scheduled → Faculty Notified of Deadline → Question Papers Collected (Hard + Soft) → Signature Verified → Sealed in A3 Envelopes → Room Arranged → Examination Conducted (Course Teacher Present) → Papers Returned for Marking → Records Filed

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: FYDP templates and guidelines (distributed to students).

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department.
Reporting frequency: An end-of-semester examination report is submitted after results are finalized; FYDP-related reports are submitted on completion of each defense cycle.

The Head of the Committee is accountable for the integrity and timeliness of the examination process and for approving examination schedules in coordination with the Chairman of the Department. Members of the Committee are responsible for question-paper handling, invigilation logistics, and record-keeping. The Chairman of the Department is the approving authority for examination schedules and major examination-related decisions.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee: Hands over examination records after conduct; receives result scrutiny outcomes.
PSAC / BAETE Committee: Provides examination evidence for accreditation.
Teaching Load Committee: Cross-checks course-teacher assignments against examination duties.
Meeting Committee: Reports FYDP schedule decisions for inclusion in departmental meeting records.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Result tabulation (handled by the Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee).
Course registration (handled by the Course Registration Committee).

committees.name: Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee
committees.tags: Result Verification | Script Scrutiny | Accuracy & Integrity

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee is responsible for verifying the accuracy and integrity of examination result sheets prepared by Faculty Members before final submission, minimizing the risk of errors in result preparation and publication.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Scrutiny of result sheets (draft/buffer-state) prepared by faculty before final university management information system (UMIS) submission.
Verification of examination scripts to confirm marking consistency.
Identification and correction of calculation or data-entry errors.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead the Committee's scrutiny process and ensure draft results are reviewed before final submission deadlines.
Coordinate the preparation of a standard scrutiny checklist and communicate submission deadlines to Faculty Members.
Escalate systematic or recurring errors to the Chairman of the Department immediately.
Approve the end-of-semester scrutiny summary report before submission.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Receive draft/buffer-state result sheets or equivalent records from Faculty Members.
Cross-check mark entries against answer scripts and verify total marks, grade boundaries, and pass/fail determinations.
Communicate identified discrepancies to the concerned Faculty Member for correction.
Maintain the scrutiny log and issue verification confirmations after satisfactory review.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The Committee verifies examination scripts and scrutinizes result sheets prepared by Faculty Members before final result submission, to minimize errors.
A draft result is prepared and submitted to the Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee for verification before the Faculty Member submits the final result.

Where a separately printed draft is not available from the university system, the buffer-state result may be captured (for example, by screenshot) and submitted to the Committee for verification; after satisfactory verification, the Faculty Member may proceed to submit the final result.
Develop a standard scrutiny checklist for result sheets (course code, marks distribution, total, grade, CGPA impact where applicable).
Maintain a log of all scrutinized results per semester, noting any corrections made.
Set and communicate the deadline for submission of draft results to the Committee.
Issue a verification confirmation to the concerned Faculty Member after scrutiny is complete.
Prepare a brief end-of-semester scrutiny summary report for submission to the Chairman of the Department.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Notify Faculty Members of the draft-result submission deadline each semester.
Receive draft/buffer-state result sheets or screenshots from Faculty Members.
Cross-check mark entries against answer scripts.
Verify total marks, grade boundaries, and pass/fail determinations.
Communicate identified discrepancies to the concerned Faculty Member for correction.
Confirm final accuracy before the Faculty Member proceeds to UMIS submission.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Faculty Marks Scripts → Prepares Draft/Buffer Result → Submits Draft (or Screenshot) to Committee → Committee Reviews → Discrepancies Identified (if any) → Faculty Corrects → Committee Re-verifies → Confirmation Issued → Faculty Submits Final Result to UMIS

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: Scrutiny confirmation record (per course, per semester).

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: Draft result submissions received (course code, date).
Correction requests sent and responses received.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department.
Reporting frequency: Once per examination cycle; systematic errors are escalated to the Chairman of the Department immediately.

The Head of the Committee, together with Members of the Committee, is responsible for verifying results before submission. The Chairman of the Department is the final approving authority for escalated issues.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Examination Committee: Receives post-examination records; returns verification outcomes.
Academic Committee: Informed if systemic assessment issues are identified.
BAETE Committee / PSAC: Provides result-accuracy evidence for accreditation.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Question-paper management (handled by the Examination Committee).
FYDP evaluation (handled by the Examination Committee).

committees.name: Laboratory Management Committee
committees.tags: Laboratory Status | Upgradation | OBE | BAETE | Manuals

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Laboratory Management Committee oversees the condition, development and operational readiness of all departmental laboratories, ensuring that facilities are adequate for delivering the OBE curriculum and meet the documentation and physical requirements for BAETE accreditation.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Assessment of laboratory condition and equipment status.
Planning and coordination of laboratory upgradation.
Preparation of laboratory status, development and budget reports.
Development of standardized laboratory manuals aligned with the OBE curriculum.
Monitoring laboratory readiness for each semester, particularly for newly admitted batches.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead the preparation of the comprehensive laboratory status and development report, covering existing conditions, required improvements, and estimated budget for upgradation.
Coordinate with the Chairman of the Department on review of the Laboratory Upgradation Report and preparation of updated laboratory manuals.
Submit the final Laboratory Upgradation Report to the Chairman of the Department for review and approval.
Monitor overall laboratory readiness before the commencement of each semester.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Collect laboratory status information from Faculty Members responsible for each laboratory room.
Inspect and document the current condition of each laboratory.
Coordinate preparation of standardized laboratory manuals with relevant Faculty Members.
Review manuals for OBE alignment (experiment objectives, PLO mapping, assessment criteria).

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: A comprehensive laboratory status and development report is prepared, covering existing conditions, required improvements, and estimated budget for upgradation to support the OBE curriculum, with Faculty Members responsible for individual laboratory rooms contributing the necessary information.
The Chairman of the Department reviews the Laboratory Upgradation Report and discusses preparation of updated laboratory manuals with the responsible Member of the Committee.
Updated laboratory manuals are prepared with consideration of BAETE accreditation requirements.

Each concerned Faculty Member may determine the detailed method of conducting laboratory classes based on course requirements and available facilities, while the Department maintains a standard laboratory manual.
Maintain an up-to-date inventory of all laboratory equipment (item, quantity, condition, year of acquisition).
Identify equipment that requires repair, replacement, or addition to support curriculum experiments.
Prepare a prioritized list of laboratory development requirements for each academic year.
Coordinate with the Departmental Budget Committee to include laboratory requirements in the annual budget proposal.
Review and update laboratory manuals in alignment with revised syllabi before each semester.
Ensure each laboratory course has a standardized manual available to students.
Monitor whether OBE-aligned experiments (including open-ended experiments as per BAETE requirements) are being conducted.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Collect laboratory status information from Faculty Members responsible for each laboratory room.
Inspect and document the current condition of each laboratory.
Compile the Laboratory Status and Development Report.
Prepare an equipment requirements list and submit it to the Budget Committee.
Coordinate preparation of standardized laboratory manuals with relevant Faculty Members.
Review manuals for OBE alignment (experiment objectives, PLO mapping, assessment criteria).
Submit the final Laboratory Upgradation Report to the Chairman of the Department.
Monitor laboratory readiness before the commencement of each semester.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Faculty Reports on Lab Rooms → Committee Inspects/Compiles → Status Report Drafted → Budget Requirements Identified → Submitted to Budget Committee → Upgradation Actions → Manual Preparation → OBE/BAETE Compliance Check → Semester Readiness Confirmation

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: Laboratory Status and Development Report (per cycle/annually).
OBE experiment mapping per laboratory course.

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: Faculty contribution records for lab status reporting.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with budget-related outputs shared with the Departmental Budget Committee and BAETE-relevant documentation shared with the BAETE Committee.
Reporting frequency: The Laboratory Status and Development Report is submitted to the Chairman of the Department on a periodic and as-needed basis, with semester readiness verified before each term.

The designated responsible Member of the Committee for laboratory affairs is accountable for preparing and updating the Laboratory Status and Development Report. The Chairman of the Department reviews and approves the Laboratory Upgradation Report. Individual Faculty Members responsible for their respective laboratory rooms are accountable for providing accurate status information.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: BAETE Committee: Provides laboratory evidence for accreditation (equipment, manuals, OBE experiment compliance).
Departmental Budget Committee: Submits laboratory budget requirements.
PSAC: Shares laboratory compliance data for self-assessment reports.
Syllabus Committee: Receives updated syllabi for laboratory-manual revision.
Teaching Load Committee: Coordinates faculty assignments for laboratory supervision.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
FYDP evaluation (handled by the Examination Committee).
Result scrutiny (handled by the Tabulation & Scrutiny Committee).
Broader accreditation submission (handled by the BAETE Committee).

committees.name: Teaching Load Committee
committees.tags: Course Distribution | Workload Balancing | Faculty Assignment

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Teaching Load Committee is responsible for the fair and systematic distribution of teaching assignments among Faculty Members, ensuring that workloads are balanced, all required courses are covered, and teaching duties are aligned with faculty qualifications and expertise.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Collection of faculty availability and qualification data.
Calculation and distribution of teaching loads per semester.
Identification of overload, underload, or coverage gaps.
Coordination with the Routine and Syllabus Committees on course offerings.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead the preparation of the semester teaching-load distribution and ensure it is submitted for review by the Chairman of the Department.
Identify coverage gaps and escalate them to the Chairman of the Department.
Approve the final teaching-load statement issued to each Faculty Member.
Ensure the finalized load distribution is communicated to the Routine Committee in time for scheduling.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Circulate the faculty availability and preference form at the start of each semester planning cycle.
Compile faculty responses and cross-reference them with the approved course list.
Match faculty qualifications and expertise to course requirements.
Maintain a record of semester-wise teaching assignments.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Collect faculty availability declarations at the beginning of each semester.
Review the approved course list for the semester (from the Syllabus/Academic Committee).
Match faculty qualifications and expertise to course requirements.
Prepare a draft teaching-load distribution for the semester.
Identify any gaps in coverage (unfilled courses) and escalate to the Chairman of the Department.
Prepare the official semester teaching-load statement for each Faculty Member.
Review and flag situations where a Faculty Member's load deviates significantly from the departmental norm.
Update the load distribution if a Faculty Member is added, leaves, or goes on study leave during the semester.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Circulate a faculty availability and preference form at the start of each semester planning cycle.
Compile faculty responses and cross-reference them with the approved course list.
Draft teaching-load assignments and share them with the Chairman of the Department for review.
Finalize the teaching-load distribution after approval.
Communicate individual load statements to each Faculty Member.
Maintain a record of semester-wise teaching assignments.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Approved Course List Received → Faculty Availability Collected → Qualification/Expertise Check → Draft Load Distribution → Review by the Chairman of the Department → Approval → Final Load Statement Issued → Communicated to Faculty and the Routine Committee

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with teaching-load statements shared with the Routine Committee to facilitate scheduling.
Reporting frequency: Once per semester, before the routine is finalized.

The Head of the Committee is accountable for the fairness and completeness of the load distribution and reports to the Chairman of the Department. Members of the Committee, supported by the Departmental Coordinator, are responsible for data collection and drafting.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Routine Committee: Provides finalized teaching assignments for schedule preparation.
Syllabus Committee / Academic Committee: Receives the approved course list.
PSAC: May need to confirm that OBE-compliant faculty are assigned to relevant courses.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Preparation of the class routine (handled by the Routine Committee).
Course registration support (handled by the Course Registration Committee).

committees.name: Routine Committee
committees.tags: Class Schedule | Room Allocation | Laboratory Scheduling

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Routine Committee is responsible for preparing and publishing the departmental class routine for each semester, ensuring that all courses (theory and laboratory) are scheduled without conflicts, rooms are allocated appropriately, and both regular and evening programs are accommodated.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Preparation of theory and laboratory class schedules.
Coordination between regular and evening program schedules.
Revision of routines when required during the semester.
Publication and communication of the approved routine.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead preparation of the draft class routine, ensuring no double-booking of faculty, rooms, or laboratories.
Circulate the draft routine for faculty review and incorporate feedback.
Submit the finalized routine to the Chairman of the Department for approval.
Coordinate handling of routine revision requests during the semester.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Obtain the course-faculty assignment list from the Teaching Load Committee.
Check room availability (theory rooms and laboratories) with the administrative office.
Draft the routine using scheduling logic to avoid conflicts.
Publish and archive the final routine.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Collect the finalized teaching-load assignments from the Teaching Load Committee.
Collect room availability from the concerned administrative office.
Prepare a draft class routine ensuring no double-booking of faculty, rooms, or laboratories.
Give specific attention to evening-program scheduling, including any multi-day class arrangements under departmental discussion.
Circulate the draft routine to Faculty Members for review.
Incorporate feedback and finalize the routine.
Submit the routine to the Chairman of the Department for approval.
Publish the approved routine through the departmental notice board and/or online channels.
Handle routine revision requests during the semester and communicate approved changes.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Obtain the course-faculty assignment list from the Teaching Load Committee.
Check room availability (theory rooms and laboratories).
Draft the routine using scheduling logic to avoid conflicts.
Publish and archive the final routine.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Teaching Load Finalized → Course List Received → Room Availability Checked → Draft Routine Prepared → Conflict Check → Faculty Review → Revisions → Approval by the Chairman of the Department → Final Routine Published → Archived

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: Revised routine (if mid-semester changes are required).

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: Draft and final routines per semester.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with the approved routine shared with Faculty Members, the Course Registration Committee, and the notice board.
The Head of the Committee is accountable for the accuracy and timely publication of the routine. The Chairman of the Department reviews and approves the final routine.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Teaching Load Committee: Receives faculty-course assignments.
Course Registration Committee: Shares the routine so students can plan course registration.
Laboratory Management Committee: Confirms laboratory availability for scheduling.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Course registration (handled by the Course Registration Committee).
Teaching-load calculation (handled by the Teaching Load Committee).

committees.name: Course Registration Committee
committees.tags: Registration Support | Course Offerings | Student Queries

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Course Registration Committee supports the course registration process by providing information on available courses, prerequisites, and sections, assisting students with registration-related queries, and coordinating with the university's registration system and administrative office.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Support for the student course registration process each semester.
Communication of approved course offerings and section capacities.
Prerequisite verification support (in coordination with academic records).

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Coordinate publication of the offered course list with credit details and prerequisites.
Oversee resolution of student registration queries and escalate capacity issues to the Chairman of the Department.
Coordinate with the Routine Committee to ensure the routine is available before registration closes.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Process registration corrections with relevant documentation.
Maintain a registration support log each semester.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Prepare and publish the list of offered courses for each semester (after Academic Committee approval).
Communicate pre-registration information to students (dates, procedures, prerequisites).
Assist students with prerequisite-related queries during the registration period.
Maintain records of section capacities and report capacity issues to the Chairman of the Department.
Coordinate with the Routine Committee to ensure students are informed of the class routine before registration closes.
Handle and process course add/drop requests in coordination with the administrative office.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Publish the offered course list with credit details and prerequisites.
Monitor section capacity and escalate capacity issues.
Process registration corrections with relevant documentation.
Maintain a registration support log each semester.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Course List Approved → Offered Courses Published → Student Registration Opens → Student Queries Handled → Prerequisite Checks → Section Capacity Monitored → Add/Drop Requests Processed → Registration Closed → Corrections Handled → Records Filed

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with administrative-level issues escalated to the Chairman of the Department and Departmental Coordinator.
Reporting frequency: Once per registration cycle.
The Head of the Committee, supported by the Departmental Coordinator, is responsible for the accuracy and timeliness of registration support activities.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Routine Committee: Coordinates timing of routine publication before registration.
Academic Committee: Receives approved course offerings.
Administrative Office / registration system: Coordinates on system-level registration matters.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Operation of the university registration system (a university function).
Preparation of class routines (handled by the Routine Committee).

committees.name: Industrial Attachment Committee (BAETE Requirement)
committees.tags: BAETE Requirement | Internship | Industry Placement | Evidence

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Industrial Attachment Committee manages the planning, placement, supervision, evaluation and documentation of student industrial attachments (internships), which are a mandatory component of the curriculum and a specific requirement for BAETE accreditation.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: All aspects of student industrial attachment/internship management.
Maintenance of an industry/organization database for placement.
Monitoring and evaluation of students during attachment.
Documentation of all industrial attachment activities as BAETE accreditation evidence.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Coordinate identification of eligible students and matching with host organizations.
Obtain departmental/university approval for placements and issue official attachment letters.
Oversee monitoring of student progress during attachment and evaluation of final reports.
Maintain and update the BAETE industrial attachment evidence portfolio.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Contact prospective host organizations and maintain the industry partner database.
Brief students on attachment requirements, conduct, and reporting.
Conduct mid-period monitoring check-ins with students/supervisors.
Collect industry feedback forms and issue completion records.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Identify and maintain a database of industry partners willing to host students for industrial attachment.
Establish and publish guidelines for industrial attachment (eligibility, duration, conduct, reporting requirements).
Match eligible students with suitable companies/organizations based on academic performance and specialization.
Obtain departmental/university approval for each student placement.
Maintain communication with industry supervisors during the attachment period.
Collect and evaluate student industrial attachment reports.
Collect industry feedback forms from hosting organizations.
Issue completion certificates/records upon successful completion.
Maintain a comprehensive industrial attachment portfolio as BAETE evidence.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Identify eligible students each semester/year (academic standing, credit completion).
Arrange student-company matching and obtain departmental approval.
Brief students on attachment requirements, conduct, and reporting.
Issue official attachment letters to companies.
Monitor attachment progress (mid-period check-in with students/supervisors).
Collect and evaluate final student reports and industry feedback.
Issue completion records and update the industrial attachment portfolio for BAETE documentation.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Eligible Students Identified → Industry Database Consulted → Student-Company Matching → Department/University Approval → Official Placement Letter Issued → Attachment Begins → Mid-Period Monitoring → Student Report Submitted → Evaluated → Industry Feedback Collected → Completion Record Issued → BAETE Portfolio Updated

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with BAETE-related documentation shared with the BAETE Committee.
Reporting frequency: Once per industrial attachment cycle (typically annual or as per curriculum requirement).

The Head of the Committee coordinates placement activities; the Chairman of the Department and Departmental Coordinator are the approving authority for placement decisions. BAETE documentation is reviewed by the BAETE Committee.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: BAETE Committee: Provides the industrial attachment portfolio as accreditation evidence.
Academic Committee: Confirms student eligibility and credit completion.
Industrial Advisory Panel: May suggest suitable industry partners.
PSAC: Industrial attachment data contributes to PLO attainment evidence.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Organizing general industrial tours (an AEEC / OBE-activity function).
Managing the Industrial Advisory Panel (a separate entity).

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Academic Advisory Panel provides external academic expertise to support the continuous improvement of the academic programme, including curriculum benchmarking, OBE alignment, research collaboration opportunities, and academic quality enhancement.

sections.title: Reference Points
blocks: Panel membership is subject to ongoing departmental review, with candidates included or excluded based on availability and interest, and additional members put forward by the Chairman of the Department.
Representatives from private universities may be considered for inclusion, subject to discussion with the Departmental Advisor.
A meeting with alumni will be arranged to discuss potential involvement and identify suitable members for the advisory panels.
The Department will review the current website structure to explore appropriate provisions for displaying the Academic Advisory Panel and Industrial Advisory Panel.

sections.title: Functions
blocks: Review and provide feedback on the curriculum from an academic benchmarking perspective.
Advise on OBE framework implementation, programme outcomes, and curriculum alignment with national and international standards.
Provide recommendations on emerging areas to be incorporated into the curriculum.
Facilitate research collaboration opportunities between the Department and other academic institutions.
Participate in annual or bi-annual advisory panel meetings.
Provide written feedback/recommendations after each meeting for departmental records.

sections.title: Key Outputs
blocks: Written feedback reports on curriculum and academic quality.

sections.title: Key Outputs
blocks: Written industry feedback on curriculum relevance.
List of suggested industry speakers, internship hosts, and collaboration partners.

sections.title: Reporting and Coordination (Both Panels)
blocks: Both advisory panels report their recommendations to the Chairman of the Department. Recommendations are subsequently reviewed by the Academic Committee, PSAC, and Syllabus Committee as appropriate, at least once per academic year or as called by the Chairman of the Department.

sections.title: Accountability
blocks: The Chairman of the Department is responsible for convening advisory panel meetings, with the Departmental Coordinator supporting coordination. Panel members are external advisors and have no administrative authority over the Department.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: Both Advisory Panels are consultative bodies. They have no administrative or decision-making authority over the Department; their role is limited to providing recommendations for consideration by the Chairman of the Department and relevant committees.

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Industrial Advisory Panel brings industry expertise to the Department, providing guidance on the relevance of the curriculum to industry requirements, employability of graduates, emerging technologies, and opportunities for collaboration.

sections.title: Reference Points
blocks: Panel membership is subject to ongoing departmental review, with candidates included or excluded based on availability of communication.
The Department will explore expanding both advisory panels with additional qualified members, including suitable alumni.

sections.title: Functions
blocks: Advise on the relevance of the curriculum to current and emerging industry requirements.
Provide feedback on graduate employability and skill gaps.
Suggest inclusion of industry-relevant content, tools, and technologies in the curriculum.
Identify opportunities for industrial attachment, internship, and industrial tours.
Suggest industry professionals for guest lectures, technical seminars, and workshops.
Advise on industry-academia collaboration and consultancy opportunities.
Provide input on employment trends relevant to graduates.

sections.title: Key Outputs
blocks: Written industry feedback on curriculum relevance.
List of suggested industry speakers, internship hosts, and collaboration partners.

sections.title: Reporting and Coordination (Both Panels)
blocks: Both advisory panels report their recommendations to the Chairman of the Department. Recommendations are subsequently reviewed by the Academic Committee, PSAC, and Syllabus Committee as appropriate, at least once per academic year or as called by the Chairman of the Department.

sections.title: Accountability
blocks: The Chairman of the Department is responsible for convening advisory panel meetings, with the Departmental Coordinator supporting coordination. Panel members are external advisors and have no administrative authority over the Department.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: Both Advisory Panels are consultative bodies. They have no administrative or decision-making authority over the Department; their role is limited to providing recommendations for consideration by the Chairman of the Department and relevant committees.

committees.name: Academic Committee
committees.tags: Academic Policy | Planning | Course Offerings | Student Matters

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Academic Committee is the primary departmental body for academic planning, policy coordination, and oversight of semester-wise academic activities. It coordinates among the various academic sub-committees and makes recommendations to the Chairman of the Department on academic matters that require departmental decision.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Academic planning and policy coordination at the departmental level.
Approval of course offerings and semester academic plans.
Coordination among the PSAC, Syllabus Committee, Teaching Load Committee, and Routine Committee.
Review of student academic matters requiring departmental decision.
OBE implementation coordination at the departmental level.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Convene and chair periodic Academic Committee meetings each semester.
Review the draft course list and academic calendar for approval.
Coordinate with the Chairman of the Department on academic decisions requiring authority.
Review Syllabus Committee proposals for curriculum changes before escalation.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Review PSAC self-assessment reports and provide input.
Participate in the review of student academic matters.
Support maintenance of Academic Committee meeting minutes.
Coordinate with sub-committees on assigned academic matters.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The Academic Committee receives the revised Departmental Mission and Vision from the PSAC for review before it is forwarded to the Syllabus/Curriculum Committee.
Review and approve the list of courses to be offered each semester.
Coordinate the implementation of the OBE curriculum across the Department.
Review and recommend academic policies for the programme.
Review cases of student academic difficulty or disputes and make recommendations to the Chairman of the Department.
Review proposals from the Syllabus Committee regarding curriculum changes before escalation.
Monitor the overall academic performance of the Department.
Coordinate with the PSAC on quality improvement actions.
Provide guidance on academic matters raised by Faculty Members.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Hold periodic meetings each semester to review academic activities.
Review the draft course list and academic calendar.
Receive and review PSAC self-assessment reports.
Review Syllabus Committee proposals for curriculum changes.
Coordinate with the Chairman of the Department on academic decisions requiring authority.
Maintain minutes of Academic Committee meetings.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Academic Issue/Proposal Raised → Referred to Academic Committee → Discussion and Review → Recommendation Prepared → Submitted to the Chairman of the Department → Decision/Approval → Communicated to Relevant Committee/Faculty → Implemented

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department.
Reporting frequency: As required; at least once per semester.
The Head of the Committee, supported by the Departmental Coordinator, is accountable for the quality of academic recommendations and coordination among sub-committees.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: PSAC: Receives self-assessment reports; coordinates OBE activities.
Teaching Load Committee: Approves course offerings for load calculation.
Routine Committee: Provides approved course list.
Course Registration Committee: Provides approved offerings for publication.
Credit Transfer Committee: Reviews recommendations on credit transfer cases.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Developing syllabi (handled by the Syllabus Committee).
Managing examinations (handled by the Examination Committee).

committees.name: FB + Website Committee
committees.tags: Social Media | Departmental Website | Official Communication

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The FB + Website Committee is responsible for maintaining and updating the Department's official social media presence and departmental website, ensuring that accurate, approved information about academic programmes, faculty, events, research, and achievements is communicated to students, applicants, alumni, and the public.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Management of the departmental social media page.
Maintenance and updating of the departmental website.
Content collection, verification, and publication workflow.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Approve or route content requests for review before publication.
Coordinate the periodic review of the website for outdated information.
Ensure the Advisory Panel section of the website is updated once memberships are finalized.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Receive content requests from Faculty Members, committees, and the Chairman of the Department.
Verify factual accuracy with the source committee or Faculty Member.
Publish approved content on social media and/or the website.
Archive published content with date and approval record.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The Department will review the current website structure and explore appropriate provisions for displaying the Academic Advisory Panel and Industrial Advisory Panel.
Establish and maintain a content publication workflow requiring departmental approval for sensitive/official content.
Collect content from relevant committees and Faculty Members (achievements, events, research, notices).
Verify accuracy of all information before publication.
Update faculty profiles, committee information, and programme details on the website.
Post approved departmental announcements, event notices, and achievements on social media.
Ensure admission-related information published online is consistent with officially approved content.
Update the Advisory Panel section of the website when memberships are finalized.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Receive content requests from faculty, committees, and the Chairman of the Department.
Verify factual accuracy with the source committee or Faculty Member.
Obtain approval from the Chairman of the Department (or designated approver) for sensitive content.
Publish approved content on social media and/or website.
Archive published content with date and approval record.
Periodically review the website for outdated information and request updates.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Content Generated (Faculty/Committee/Event) → Submitted to FB + Website Committee → Accuracy Verified → Approval Obtained → Published (Social Media / Website) → Archived with Date and Approver Record → Outdated Content Reviewed and Updated

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: Updated website pages (faculty, programmes, events, research, committees).

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: Publication log (date, content, platform, approved by).

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department; administrative decisions on unverified content requests are escalated to the Chairman of the Department.
Reporting frequency: As required; a quarterly review of website content is recommended.

The Head of the Committee coordinates the publication workflow. The approving authority for content is the Chairman of the Department (or a designated Faculty Member). Individual Faculty Members are responsible for the accuracy of their own profiles.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: All committees: Receive content for publication (events, achievements, updates).
BAETE Committee: Ensures accreditation-relevant information is accurately reflected on the website.
AEEC coordination: Publishes club activities and student achievements.
Laboratory Management Committee: Ensures laboratory information on the website is current.
Advisory Panels: Updates advisory panel membership once finalized.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Making independent academic or administrative decisions — all content must be approved before publication.

committees.name: Syllabus Committee
committees.tags: Curriculum Development | Syllabus Revision | OBE | BAETE Alignment

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Syllabus Committee is responsible for reviewing, developing and revising the departmental curriculum and individual course syllabi, ensuring alignment with OBE principles, BAETE accreditation requirements, and current academic and industry standards.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: CLO (Course Learning Outcome) and PLO (Programme Learning Outcome) alignment.
Incorporation of industry and academic advisory feedback into the curriculum.
Submission of revised curriculum for departmental approval through proper channels.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Coordinate collection of curriculum feedback from relevant panels, committees, and faculty.
Lead the review of existing syllabi for OBE compliance and oversee drafting of revised syllabi.
Submit finalized curriculum proposals to the Academic Committee.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Circulate drafts to relevant Faculty Members and committees for feedback.
Support coordination with the Laboratory Management Committee on laboratory course content alignment.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The semester-wise fixed course distribution is prepared during the syllabus development and submission process, with the semester-wise course list provided to the Department for further reference and implementation.
The revised Departmental Mission and Vision, once prepared by the PSAC, is submitted to the Syllabus/Curriculum Committee for further consideration.
Conduct periodic review of the curriculum (at least once per academic year or before each accreditation cycle).
Collect feedback from the Academic Advisory Panel, Industrial Advisory Panel, PSAC, and BAETE Committee on curriculum relevance and gaps.
Prepare revised course syllabi with updated CLOs and PLO mappings.
Ensure the credit structure conforms to university and BAETE requirements.
Review and update prerequisite structures for all courses.
Coordinate with the Laboratory Management Committee to align laboratory course content with curriculum revisions.
Submit curriculum changes to the Academic Committee for review before university-level approval.
Maintain a version history of all curricula.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Collect curriculum feedback from relevant panels, committees, and faculty.
Review existing syllabi for OBE compliance (CLO-PLO mapping, assessment alignment).
Draft revised syllabi or new course proposals.
Circulate drafts to relevant faculty and committees for feedback.
Finalize and submit to the Academic Committee.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Feedback Collected (PSAC, Advisory Panels, Faculty) → Curriculum Review → CLO/PLO Gap Analysis → Revised Syllabus Drafted → Faculty/Committee Review → Academic Committee Submission → University Approval Process → Implementation → Documentation

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: All versions of the curriculum and individual syllabi.
Submission records to the Academic Committee and university.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Academic Committee and Chairman of the Department; final curriculum revisions are submitted through the university's curriculum approval process.
Reporting frequency: As required; at least annually.
The Head of the Committee is reviewed by the Academic Committee, with final approval resting with the university authority per the university's curriculum approval process.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Academic Committee: Submits revised curriculum for departmental review.
PSAC: Receives self-assessment feedback on curriculum effectiveness; provides OBE alignment guidance.
BAETE Committee: Ensures curriculum meets BAETE accreditation standards.
Academic Advisory Panel: Provides external academic feedback.
Industrial Advisory Panel: Provides industry relevance feedback.
Laboratory Management Committee: Coordinates laboratory course content.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Implementing the curriculum (handled by the PSAC/Academic Committee).
Managing examinations (handled by the Examination Committee).
Making final accreditation submissions (handled by the BAETE Committee).

committees.name: Credit Transfer Committee
committees.tags: Credit Evaluation | Course Equivalency | Transcript Review

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Credit Transfer Committee evaluates requests from students seeking to transfer credits earned at other institutions, determining course equivalency and making recommendations to the Chairman of the Department on the number and type of credits to be recognized.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Evaluation of student credit transfer requests.
Preparation of recommendations for the Chairman of the Department.
Documentation of all credit transfer decisions.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Oversee verification of transcript authenticity and course-equivalency analysis.
Review and finalize recommendation reports before submission to the Chairman of the Department.
Ensure the credit transfer register is kept up to date.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Receive and acknowledge credit transfer applications and supporting documents.
Compare course titles, content, credit hours, and learning outcomes with the programme curriculum.
Communicate the decision to the student in writing after approval.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Receive and acknowledge credit transfer requests from students.
Collect the student's official transcript and course descriptions from the prior institution.
Compare course titles, content, credit hours, and learning outcomes with the programme curriculum.
Prepare a course equivalency assessment for each requested credit transfer.
Prepare a formal recommendation (approved/rejected/partial) for submission to the Chairman of the Department.
Communicate the decision to the student in writing after approval by the Chairman of the Department.
Maintain a register of all credit transfer applications and decisions.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Receive credit transfer application and supporting documents.
Verify authenticity of transcripts and course descriptions.
Submit to the Chairman of the Department for approval.
Communicate the outcome to the student.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Student Applies → Documents Received and Verified → Course Equivalency Analysis → Recommendation Prepared → Submitted to the Chairman of the Department → Approval/Rejection Decision → Student Notified → Register Updated → Records Filed

sections.title: Key Outputs / Deliverables
blocks: Recommendations submitted to the Chairman of the Department.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department; recommendations are submitted per individual application.
Reporting frequency: As required, per application.

The Head of the Committee is responsible for the accuracy of equivalency assessments. The Chairman of the Department is the approving authority for credit transfer recommendations at the departmental level, subject to university policy.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Academic Committee: Referred for complex cases involving significant credit volumes.
Syllabus Committee: May be consulted on curriculum equivalency for new courses.
Administrative Office: Coordinates recording of credits after approval.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Independent authority to grant credit transfers — the Committee makes recommendations only.
Setting university credit-transfer policy (a university authority).
Note: The Committee should not apply a credit-transfer policy of its own; any equivalency decisions must be consistent with the university's official credit-transfer rules.

committees.name: BAETE Committee
committees.tags: BAETE Accreditation | Documentation | Compliance | Evidence Portfolio

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The BAETE Committee is the dedicated accreditation coordination body of the Department, responsible for preparing, compiling, and maintaining all documentation, evidence and compliance materials required for BAETE (Board of Accreditation for Engineering and Technical Education) accreditation of the programme.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Overall coordination of BAETE accreditation activities.
Compilation of accreditation documentation (programme details, faculty, students, facilities, outcomes, CQI).
Evidence collection from all departmental committees for accreditation purposes.
Monitoring ongoing compliance with BAETE criteria between accreditation visits.
Coordination with the PSAC for self-assessment data.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Lead the review of the BAETE accreditation manual and update the Department's compliance checklist.
Assign evidence collection responsibilities to each committee and oversee compilation into the Self-Evaluation Report.
Coordinate mock accreditation reviews and BAETE site-visit preparation.
Track and follow up on pending evidence items and post-visit recommendations.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Compile evidence received into the BAETE documentation portfolio.
Maintain course-file evidence, faculty qualification records, and student performance records.
Update the portfolio after each self-assessment cycle.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Updated laboratory manuals are prepared with consideration of BAETE accreditation requirements.
Standardized laboratory manuals are recognized as important for BAETE accreditation.
Maintain an up-to-date knowledge of BAETE accreditation criteria and requirements.
Prepare and maintain the BAETE Self-Evaluation Report (SER).
Collect and compile evidence from all relevant committees (PSAC, Laboratory Management, Examination, Industrial Attachment, and others).
Coordinate preparation of Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs) and Programme Learning Outcomes (PLOs).
Maintain course-file evidence (assessment evidence, CLO attainment, CQI records).
Maintain records of faculty qualifications, research, and professional development.
Maintain student performance and attainment records.
Prepare the Department for BAETE accreditation site visits.
Track and implement BAETE's post-visit recommendations.
Liaise with the IQAC and university-level accreditation coordination bodies.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Review the current BAETE accreditation manual and update the Department's compliance checklist.
Assign evidence collection responsibilities to each committee.
Compile evidence received into the BAETE documentation portfolio.
Track and follow up on pending evidence items.
Update the portfolio after each self-assessment cycle.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: BAETE Criteria Review → Evidence Requirements Mapped to Committees → Evidence Collected → Compiled into SER → Internal Review → Approval by the Chairman of the Department → University Submission → BAETE Visit Preparation → Post-Visit Action Tracking

sections.title: Records and Documentation
blocks: Evidence items by criterion and source committee.

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department and the IQAC.
Reporting frequency: Continuous during accreditation preparation; annually during maintenance cycles.
The Head of the Committee is accountable to the Chairman of the Department and the IQAC. All departmental committees are jointly accountable for providing accurate evidence to the BAETE Committee.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: PSAC: Provides self-assessment data and CQI evidence.
Laboratory Management Committee: Provides laboratory evidence (equipment, manuals, OBE experiments).
Examination Committee: Provides assessment evidence and FYDP records.
Industrial Attachment Committee: Provides industrial attachment records.
Syllabus Committee: Provides curriculum documents and CLO-PLO mappings.
IQAC: Reports progress; receives guidance on accreditation matters.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Independently developing the curriculum (handled by the Syllabus Committee).
Managing laboratories (handled by the Laboratory Management Committee).
Conducting programme self-assessment (handled by the PSAC) — the BAETE Committee coordinates and compiles.

Note: Distinction: the PSAC conducts ongoing programme self-assessment and quality monitoring; the BAETE Committee compiles and manages the formal accreditation documentation and submission process. They work closely together but serve distinct functions.

committees.name: Departmental Budget Committee
committees.tags: Budget Planning | Expenditure Monitoring | Resource Proposals

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Departmental Budget Committee is responsible for preparing the annual departmental budget proposal, prioritizing expenditure requirements, monitoring actual expenditure against allocations, and coordinating with the university administration on financial matters relating to the Department.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Preparation of the annual departmental budget proposal.
Collection of budget requirements from all relevant committees.
Submission of budget proposals to the appropriate university authority.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Coordinate committee activities related to budget requirement collection and prioritization.
Submit the formal budget proposal through the Chairman of the Department to the university finance office.
Track expenditure against the approved budget and prepare the year-end summary.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Issue budget requirement collection notices to all committees.
Support preparation of the formal budget proposal document.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: The Committee is responsible for the activities of the Departmental Budget Committee, as reflected in departmental decisions.
The Department will consider preparing and submitting a proposal for procuring a GPU-based laptop/workstation to support faculty research and computationally intensive academic activities.
Circulate a budget requirements collection form to all committees before the annual budget submission deadline.
Compile all requirements and prepare a prioritized budget proposal.
Submit the budget proposal to the appropriate university authority through the Chairman of the Department.
Monitor expenditure against the approved budget throughout the year.
Prepare a budget utilization report at the end of the financial year.
Coordinate with the Laboratory Management Committee for equipment budget needs.
Coordinate with the AEEC coordination body for student activity budget requirements.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Issue budget requirement collection notices to all committees.
Prioritize requirements based on departmental needs and available allocation.
Prepare the formal budget proposal document.
Submit through the Chairman of the Department to the university finance office.
Track expenditure against the approved budget.
Prepare a year-end budget utilization summary.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Requirements Collected from Committees → Compiled and Prioritized → Budget Proposal Drafted → Review by the Chairman of the Department → Submission to University Authority → Approval Received → Budget Communicated to Committees → Expenditure Monitored → Year-End Report

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department; the budget proposal is submitted to university finance/administration through the Chairman of the Department.
Reporting frequency: Annual budget cycle, with mid-year expenditure review as required.

The Head of the Committee, together with the responsible Members of the Committee, is accountable for the accuracy of the proposal. The approving authority is the university administration, not the Committee independently.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: Laboratory Management Committee: Laboratory equipment and upgradation budget.
University Finance / Administration: Submits and tracks the budget.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Independent financial approval authority — budget approval rests with the university administration.

committees.name: Meeting Committee
committees.tags: Meeting Planning | Agenda | Minutes | Action Tracking

sections.title: Purpose
blocks: The Meeting Committee supports the planning and administration of departmental meetings, including agenda preparation, meeting coordination, minute-taking, distribution of minutes, and follow-up on action items arising from meetings.

sections.title: Scope
blocks: Coordination and administration of departmental meetings.
Preparation and distribution of meeting minutes.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of the Head of the Committee
blocks: Finalize the agenda in consultation with the Chairman of the Department.
Approve draft minutes before distribution, in coordination with the Chairman of the Department.
Maintain the action-item tracker and report status at subsequent meetings.

sections.title: Roles and Responsibilities of Members of the Committee
blocks: Collect agenda items from Faculty Members and committees before each meeting.
Distribute approved minutes to all members and relevant parties.
Maintain a complete archive of all departmental meeting minutes.

sections.title: General Functional Responsibilities
blocks: Collect agenda items from Faculty Members and committees before each meeting.
Compile and finalize the agenda in consultation with the Chairman of the Department.
Issue formal meeting notices with the agenda and supporting documents.
Take accurate minutes during meetings, recording discussions, decisions, and action items.
Circulate draft minutes to the Chairman of the Department for approval.
Distribute approved minutes to all members and relevant parties.
Maintain an action-item tracker with responsible roles, deadlines, and status.
Follow up on pending action items and report status at subsequent meetings.
Maintain a complete archive of all departmental meeting minutes.

sections.title: Key Activities / Functions
blocks: Draft and circulate the final agenda with approval by the Chairman of the Department.
Draft minutes and submit them to the Chairman of the Department.
Update the action tracker after each meeting.
Report action-item status at subsequent meetings.

sections.title: Workflow / Operating Procedure
blocks: Agenda Items Collected → Agenda Finalized (Approval by the Chairman of the Department) → Meeting Notice Issued → Meeting Held → Minutes Drafted → Approval → Minutes Distributed → Action Tracker Updated → Follow-up at Next Meeting

sections.title: Reporting and Accountability
blocks: Reports to: the Chairman of the Department, with minutes distributed to all Faculty Members and relevant parties.
Reporting frequency: Action-item status is reported at each subsequent meeting; the minutes archive is maintained continuously.

The Head of the Committee is accountable for accurate minute-taking and archival. The Chairman of the Department is the approving authority for meeting agendas and minutes. All Faculty Members are responsible for providing agenda items and fulfilling action items assigned to them.

sections.title: Coordination with Other Committees/Bodies
blocks: All committees: The Committee collects agenda items from all committees.
Chairman of the Department: Approves the agenda and minutes before distribution.
Departmental Coordinator: May support logistics and distribution.

sections.title: Committee Boundaries
blocks: This Committee does NOT handle the following:
Making departmental decisions — decision-making authority rests with the Chairman of the Department and the meeting participants.

committees.name: Student Engagement & AEEC Coordination
committees.tags: Student Body | Not a Formal Departmental Committee
committees.note: Not a formal departmental committee: a student body coordinated through a Faculty Advisor.

sections.title: Role of the AEEC
blocks: The AEEC is the primary student engagement body of the Department. It organizes technical, academic, and social activities to develop students' professional skills, team engagement, and awareness of industry and academic trends.

sections.title: Responsibilities
blocks: The AEEC is assigned responsibility for organizing the Freshers' Reception for each new intake, preferably before the Midterm Examination.
The AEEC continues communicating with students through a group communication channel to identify their interests and collect suggestions for future activities.
The Club may consider organizing office-productivity software workshops based on student feedback.
The Club will explore opportunities to arrange industrial tours for students.
An engaging student activity, such as a brainstorming session or similar event, will be organized to activate and increase student participation.
A designated Faculty Member will propose a suitable date for organizing a club activity within the academic year.
The AEEC may be involved in organizing industrial visits, including participation by evening-program students.

sections.title: Coordination Framework
blocks: The Department will designate a Faculty Advisor for the AEEC to facilitate coordination between the Club and the Department.
The Club will submit activity plans to the Faculty Advisor and the Chairman of the Department for review before implementation.
The Club will maintain a record of all activities organized, including attendance and feedback.
Financial requirements for Club activities will be submitted to the Departmental Budget Committee through the Faculty Advisor.
The Club will coordinate with the FB + Website Committee to publish approved Club activities and achievements.
The Club will submit an annual activity report to the Department.

sections.title: Typical Activities
blocks: Freshers' Reception (each new intake, preferably before the Midterm Examination).
Technical workshops (office-productivity software and other relevant tools).
Academic briefing and orientation sessions for new students.
Student feedback collection for departmental improvement.

sections.title: Coordination with the Department
blocks: Club activities are coordinated through the designated Faculty Advisor. Activities with financial implications or external engagements are approved by the Chairman of the Department. The Club is not a decision-making body for academic matters.

sections.title: Accountability
blocks: The Faculty Advisor (designated by the Chairman of the Department) is responsible for coordination and guidance. The AEEC's own student leadership is responsible for organizing and executing activities. The Chairman of the Department is the approving authority for significant activities and external engagements.
